'''''Batrachospermum''''' is a [[genus]] of [[red algae]] from the family ''[[Batrachospermaceae]]''. Due to its complex [[biological life cycle]], descriptions of the taxon typically focus on [[gametophyte]]s, while [[sporophyte]]s, i.e., [[carposporophyte]]s, are filamentous structures growing on the gametophyte, on which they depend. Independently living sporophytes have sometimes been described as separate species within the genus ''{{Interlanguage link|Chantransia|pl|Szantransja}}''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Kato |first1=Aki |last2=Morita |first2=Naohiro |last3=Hiratsuka |first3=Tomoko |last4=Suda |first4=Shoichiro |year=2009 |title=Recent introduction of a freshwater red alga Chantransia macrospora (Batrachospermales, Rhodophyta) to Okinawa, Japan |url=http://www.aquaticinvasions.net/2009/index4.html |journal=Aquatic Invasions |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=565–574 |doi=10.3391/ai.2009.4.4.1|doi-access=free }}</ref> Additionally, differences may occur in the descriptions of the genus due to variations in [[Taxonomy|taxonomic]] approaches, as new taxonomic techniques, as with other [[algae]], result in changes in the assignment of individual species to the genus ''Batrachospermum''. The genus is cosmopolitan, and its representatives are found in freshwater environments, mainly rivers, and less frequently in standing waters. These plants have [[thalli]] in the form of gelatinous-coated filaments.

== Name ==
The etymology of the scientific name ({{Langx|el|βάτραχος}} – ''frog'', {{Lang|el|σπέρμα}} – ''seed'') refers to its gelatinous appearance resembling frog [[Spawn (biology)|spawn]]. The Polish name, ''żabirośl'' (frogseed) also allude to this appearance.

== Systematics and variability ==
The genus ''Batrachospermum'' was established by [[Albrecht Wilhelm Roth]] at the end of the 18th century, described in his work ''Bemerkungen über das Studium der cryptogamischen Wassergewächse'' (''Remarks on the study of cryptogamic aquatic plants''). Previously, botanists described these algae as species belonging to the genera ''[[Conferva]]'' (now not recognized, with its representatives mainly classified under the genus ''[[Cladophora]]'') – ''Conferva gelatinosa'' or ''Conferva'' ''nodosa'' ([[Carl Linnaeus]]), or [[Charales]] – ''Chara batrachosperma'' (Friedrich Wilhelm Weiss). Initially, Roth used the name ''Chara gelatinosa''.<ref name=":0" /> The [[binomial nomenclature]] were first used in 1801 by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]], who distinguished three species: ''B. gelatinosum'', ''B. simplex'', and ''B. nigricans''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=de Candolle |first=Augustin Pyramus |year=1801 |title=Extrait d'un rapport sur les conferves |journal=Bulletin des Sciences par la Société Philomathique de Paris 3 |language=fr |pages=17–21}}</ref> Thus, ''B. gelatinosum'' became the [[type species]] ([[holotype]]) of its genus, with the [[basionym]] being ''Conferva gelatinosa'' (L. 1753: 1166).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last1=Guiry |first1=G. M. |last2=Guiry |first2=M. D. |year=2012 |title=Batrachospermum Roth, 1797: 36 |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/genus/detail/?genus_id=Kbdecbd116ec4ae45 |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=www.algaebase.org |publisher=National University of Ireland |publication-place=Galway}}</ref>

In older systems (e.g., [[Engler system]]), the genera ''Batrachospermum'' and ''Chantransia'' were classified under the family ''Helminthocladiaceae'' in the order ''Nemalionales''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Engler |first=Adolf |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/63778#2 |title=Syllabus der Pflanzenfamilien |publisher=Verlag von Gebrüder Borntraeger |year=1903 |edition=3 |location=Berlin |page=20 |language=de}}</ref> Currently, the family ''Batrachospermaceae'' and the order ''Batrachospermales'' are recognized. According to some systematic proposals, this order is [[Monotypic taxon|monotypic]], and families distinguished within it, such as ''Lemaneaceae'', should be synonymized with ''Batrachospermaceae''.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Entwisle |first1=Timothy J. |last2=Vis |first2=Morgan L. |last3=Chiasson |first3=Wayne B. |last4=Necchi Jr. |first4=Orlando |last5=Sherwood |first5=Alison R. |year=2009 |title=Systematics of the Batrachospermales (Rhodophyta) — a synthesis |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1529-8817.2009.00686.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language= |volume=45 |issue=3 |pages=704–715 |doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.2009.00686.x |pmid=27034046 |bibcode=2009JPcgy..45..704E |issn=0022-3646|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Depending on the systematic approach, there are from several dozen to several hundred species within the genus.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Results of INA query |url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/search_ina?lookfor=batrachospermum |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=Index Nominum Algarum, algae, seaweeds, algal nomenclature, algal taxonomy, Paul Silva, phycology, Center for Phycological Documentation}}</ref> The development of [[molecular phylogenetics]] has challenged the traditional morphology and anatomy-based taxonomy. According to these studies, the genus ''Batrachospermum'' is [[paraphyletic]] – nested within its [[clade]] are genera such as ''[[Lemanea]]'', ''Nothocladus'', ''Paralemanea'', ''Petrohua'', ''{{Interlanguage link|Psilosiphon scoparius|pl|Psilosiphon scoparius}}'', ''Sirodotia'', and ''Tuomeya''. In order to maintain the genus as a monophyletic taxon in a broad sense, all the above-mentioned genera are included in ''Batrachospermum'', or in a narrow sense, only the [[type species]], ''B. gelatinosum'', is included, with its recognized form (sometimes elevated to the species rank) ''B. gelatinosum'' f. ''spermatoinvolucrum'' (M.L.Vis & R.G.Sheath).<ref name=":3" /> In the narrow sense, the previously distinguished sections are elevated to the rank of genera, for example, the ''Hybrida'' section (previously distinguished as the ''Contorta'' section) is raised to the genus ''Kumanoa''. According to one proposal, the paraphyletic genus ''Batrachospermum'' can be divided into the following sections:<ref name=":3" />

* ''Acarposporophytum (Batrachospermum brasiliense)''
* ''Aristata (Batrachospermum cayennense)''
* ''Batrachospermum (Batrachospermum gelatinosum)''
* ''Gonimopropagulum (Batrachospermum breutelli)''
* ''Helminthoidea (Batrachospermum arcuatum, Batrachospermum boryanum, Batrachospermum confusum, Batrachospermum heterocorticum, Batrachospermum involutum)''
* ''Macrospora (Batrachospermum macrosporum)''
* ''Setacea (Batrachospermum atrum, Batrachospermum puiggarianum)''
* ''Turfosa (Batrachospermum turfosum)''
* ''Virescentia (Batrachospermum elegans, Batrachospermum helminthosum)''

Additionally, there is a provisionally designated [[Australasia]]n group, which is paraphyletic and from which the genera ''Nothocladus'' and ''Petrohua'', as well as the ''Setacea'' section (''Batrachospermum antipodites'', ''Batrachospermum campyloclonum'', ''Batrachospermum discors'', ''Batrachospermum kraftii'', ''Batrachospermum pseudogelatinosum'', ''Batrachospermum theaquum'', ''Batrachospermum wattsii''), originate.

After the separation of the genus ''Kumanoa'', the following species formerly classified under ''Batrachospermum'' are transferred to this genus: ''B. australicum'' (''Kumanoa australica''), ''B. breviarticulatum'' (''Kumanoa breviarticulata''), ''B. cipoense'' (''Kumanoa cipoensis''), ''B. deminutum'' (''Kumanoa deminuta''), ''B. equisetoideum'' (''Kumanoa equisetoidea''), ''B. globosporum'' (''Kumanoa globospora''), ''B. gracillimum'' (''Kumanoa gracillima''), ''B. intortum'' (''Kumanoa intorta''), ''B. louisianae'' (''Kumanoa louisianae''), ''B. nodiflorum'' (''Kumanoa nodiflora''), ''B. procarpum'' (''Kumanoa procarpa''), ''B. spermatiophorum'' (''Kumanoa spermatiophora''), ''B. virgatodecaisneanum'' (''Kumanoa virgatodecaisneana''), ''B. vittatum'' (''Kumanoa vittata'').

== Morphology ==

=== Habit ===
The [[thallus]] is filamentous, covered with a slippery, gelatinous sheath, with [[mucilage]] primarily composed of [[oligosaccharide]]s.<ref name=":2" /> The degree of gelatinosity of the thallus varies between species. Species occurring in swifter currents typically have a more compact form, while those in slower currents have a looser form.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last=Necchi |first=Orlando |year=1997 |title=Microhabitat and plant structure of Batrachospermum (Batrachospermales, Rhodophyta) populations in four streams of São Paulo State, southeastern Brazil |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1440-1835.1997.tb00060.x |journal=Phycological Research |language=en |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=39–45 |doi=10.1111/j.1440-1835.1997.tb00060.x |issn=1322-0829|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The [[gametophyte]] thallus is filamentous, up to 40 cm long (usually shorter in many species), typically branching [[monopodial]]ly to [[dichotomy]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite book |last1=Szoszkiewicz |first1=Krzysztof |url=https://www.gios.gov.pl/images/dokumenty/raporty/Klucz_makrofitow_nizsza_rozdzielczosc.pdf |title=Klucz do oznaczania makrofitów dla potrzeb oceny stanu ekologicznego wód powierzchniowych |last2=Jusik |first2=Szymon |last3=Zgoła |first3=Tomasz |date=2010 |publisher=Inspekcja Ochrony Środowiska |isbn=978-83-61227-32-8 |edition=2 |series=Biblioteka Monitoringu Środowiska |location=Warsaw |pages=284–285 |language=pl}}</ref> Downward-growing filaments form the covering cortex around the central filament, sometimes resembling [[rhizoid]]s in the lower part.<ref name=":2" /> Nodes occur between the cells of the main filament, from which lateral filaments grow radially. From the cortex filaments situated on the [[internodes]], intercortical filaments also arise. Lateral cortical filaments are more branched and longer than intercortical ones. Younger thalli usually form broader branches (up to 350 μm wide) than older ones (100–200 μm).<ref name=":6" />

The color varies, ranging from brownish, olive, purple, gray to bluish-green.<ref name=":2" />

The sporophyte stage is crustose, consisting of large basal cells from which poorly branched filaments grow upwards.<ref name=":2" />

=== Anatomy ===
The cells of the main filament are elongated (150–200 μm) in shape of a cylinder. The cells of the cortical filaments are lens-shaped, ellipsoidal, up to 30 μm in length.<ref name=":6" /> Each cell contains several ribbon-shaped [[chloroplast]]s without [[pyrenoid]]s. The chloroplasts contain a single fragmented [[thylakoid]].<ref name=":2" /> Among the metabolites, in addition to substances typical for all red algae (such as red algal starch), [[trehalose]] is present.<ref name=":7">{{Cite book |last1=Gumiński |first1=Stefan |title=Fizjologia glonów i sinic |last2=Starmach |first2=Karol |date=1990 |publisher=Wydawnictwo Uniwersytetu Wrocławskiego |isbn=978-83-229-0372-8 |edition=1 |location=Wrocław |pages=78, 98 |language=pl}}</ref> The number of chromosomes (n) varies, depending on the species, ranging from 2 to 22.<ref name=":2" />

=== Structures for propagation ===
Several species produce monospores, but usually [[carpospore]]s are formed. Spermatangia (male [[Gametangium|gametangia]]) are spherical (4–8 μm in diameter) and colorless, usually clustered at the end of filaments, sometimes also on branches carrying carpogonia. Male gametes are non-motile gametangia. Female gametes – [[Carpogonium|carpogonia]] – are essentially equivalent to [[Oogonium|oogonia]]. The hair of the carpogonium is club-shaped.<ref name=":8">{{Cite book |last=Harder |first=Richard |title=Botanika: podręcznik dla szkół wyższych |publisher=PWRiL |year=1967 |editor-last=Strasburger |editor-first=Eduard |edition=2 |location=Warsaw |pages=580–585 |language=pl |chapter=Systematyka}}</ref> [[Carposporophyte]]s are roughly spherical, formed by gonimoblasts, with carposporangia at the tips (lacking [[cystocarp]]).<ref name=":8" /> In ''Batrachospermum'' ''breutelli'', the carposporophyte produces multicellular [[Diaspore (botany)|diaspores]] that detach.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sheath |first1=Robert G. |last2=Whittick |first2=Alan |year=1995 |title=The unique gonimoblast propagules of Batrachospermum breutelii (Batrachospermales, Rhodophyta) |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.2216/i0031-8884-34-1-33.1 |journal=Phycologia |language= |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=33–38 |doi=10.2216/i0031-8884-34-1-33.1 |bibcode=1995Phyco..34...33S |issn=0031-8884|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Spores do not have any [[Endospore|endosporic]] features.<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal |last1=Hall |first1=Melissa M. |last2=Vis |first2=Morgan L. |year=2002 |title=Genetic variation in Batrachospermum helminthosum (Batrachospermales, Rhodophyta) among and within stream reaches using intersimple sequence repeat molecular markers |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1046/j.1440-1835.2002.00269.x |journal=Phycological Research |language=en |volume=50 |issue=2 |pages=155–162 |doi=10.1046/j.1440-1835.2002.00269.x |issn=1322-0829|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Ecology ==
In defining environmental requirements, taxonomic controversies pose a certain difficulty. It happens that a particular species is considered by ecologists as an indicator of a certain environmental condition, while another species is considered an indicator of a different condition. However, both of these species may turn out to be synonymous to each other as a result of molecular studies.

=== Geographical distribution ===
The genus is freshwater and cosmopolitan. Since red algae are mostly found in saltwater environments, in some regions, representatives of ''Batrachospermum'' are the most common riverine red algae. This is the case with ''Batrachospermum gelatinosum'', which was found in 13% of samples collected from North American streams.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sheath |first1=Robert G. |last2=Cole |first2=Kathleen M. |year=1992 |title=Biogeography of stream macroalgae in North America |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.0022-3646.1992.00448.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language=en |volume=28 |issue=4 |pages=448–460 |doi=10.1111/j.0022-3646.1992.00448.x |bibcode=1992JPcgy..28..448S |issn=0022-3646|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In the streams of the upper [[São Francisco River|São Francisco]] basin in Brazil, various species of ''Batrachospermum'', especially in the thallus stage, are one of the most common taxonomic groups of macroalgae.<ref name=":10">{{Cite journal |last1=Necchi-Júnior |first1=O. |last2=Branco |first2=L. H. Z. |last3=Branco |first3=C. C. Z. |year=2003 |title=Ecological distribution of stream macroalgal communities from a drainage basin in the Serra da Canastra National Park, Minas Gerais, Southeastern Brazil |url=http://www.scielo.br/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S1519-69842003000400010&lng=en&tlng=en |journal=Brazilian Journal of Biology |volume=63 |issue=4 |pages=635–646 |doi=10.1590/S1519-69842003000400010 |pmid=15029374 |issn=1519-6984|hdl=11449/141871 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> In [[Poland]], occurrences are scattered throughout the country, with more frequent sightings in the [[Pomerania]] region and in the Silesian-Lesser Poland [[Highland|Uplands]].<ref name=":6" />

Some species, such as ''B. gelatinosum'', are found on all continents (except [[Antarctica]]), while others are endemic (e.g., ''Batrachospermum spermatiophorum'' known only from one stream on [[Maui Island]]),<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sherwood |first1=Alison R. |last2=Vis |first2=Morgan L. |last3=Sheath |first3=Robert G. |year=2004 |title=Phenology and phylogenetic positioning of the Hawaiian endemic freshwater alga, Batrachospermum spermatiophorum (Rhodophyta, Batrachospermales) |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1440-183.2004.00343.x |journal=Phycological Research |language=en |volume=52 |issue=3 |pages=193–203 |doi=10.1111/j.1440-183.2004.00343.x |issn=1322-0829|url-access=subscription }}</ref> although according to some proposals, it may be transferred to the genus ''Kumanoa''.

=== Habitat ===
Species of ''Batrachospermum'' inhabit the [[benthos]] of moderately to swiftly flowing waters (average flow velocity – 19 cm/s)<ref name=":2" /> with a substrate of gravelly or stony bottoms, and even in springs. They are rarely found in standing waters. The substrate to which they are attached can vary from stones to [[macrophyte]]s, especially among different species. Representatives are often [[rheophile]]s or rheobionts and live in waters with a wide range of current velocities, but with averages exceeding 40 cm/s (e.g., ''Batrachospermum boryanum''),<ref name=":11">{{Cite book |last1=Kawecka |first1=Barbara |title=Zarys ekologii glonów wód słodkich i środowisk lądowych |last2=Eloranta |first2=Pertti Vesa |publisher=Wydawnictwo Naukowe PWN |year=1994 |isbn=978-83-01-11320-9 |location=Warsaw |pages=88, 124, 193 |language=pl}}</ref> or even 50 cm/s (''B. keratophytum'', which also occurs in ponds).<ref name=":4" /> Due to the high oxygenation typical of such conditions, they exhibit characteristics of organisms highly tolerant to oxygen, and a decrease in oxygen concentration results in a decrease in respiratory rate.<ref name=":7" /> These conditions favor rapid water self-purification, especially from organic pollutants, so these species are recognized as [[saprobic system]]s (''B. vagum'') or saproxenes (''B. moniliforme'', also known as ''B. gelatinosum''),<ref name=":11" /> although the latter species may also indicate γ-mesosaprobic waters.<ref name=":12">{{Cite journal |last1=Eloranta |first1=Pertti |last2=Kwandrans |first2=Janina |year=2004 |title=Indicator value of freshwater red algae in running waters for water quality assessment |url=http://yadda.icm.edu.pl/yadda/element/bwmeta1.element.baztech-article-BUS8-0013-0005 |journal=Oceanological and Hydrobiological Studies |publisher=Uniwersytet Gdański, Instytut Oceanografii |volume=33 |issue=1 |issn=1730-413X}}</ref> They mainly occur in waters with low [[Mineral (nutrient)|mineral]] content. Unlike most algae, they do not assimilate carbon bound in carbonate ions, so they require dissolved CO<sub>2</sub>.<ref name=":6" /> As a result, despite their ability to occur in waters with different pH levels, they are more common in acidic waters,<ref name=":11" /> where such a form of inorganic carbon predominates. Some representatives (''B. keratophytum'', ''B. vagum'' – both species sometimes considered synonyms of ''B. turfosum'') occur in [[Dystrophic lake|dystrophic]] waters, with low transparency, but they can also occur in swiftly flowing waters. Even then, however, they are more common in streams with water rich in humic compounds – more acidic and darker than average.<ref name=":10" /> Also, representatives of some other species have a wide range of tolerance to sunlight, pH, and other parameters. This applies especially to ''B. gelatinosum'', the only representative of the genus occurring up to the [[tundra]] zone,<ref name=":2" /> and described under synonymous names (''B. delicatulum'') also from tropical zones.<ref name=":5" /> This species is sometimes described as typical for both eutrophic and oligotrophic waters.<ref name=":12" />

Thallus and gametophyte stages can occur in different habitat conditions.<ref name=":5" /> It happens that only one of these generations is observed in certain regions.<ref name=":1" />

=== Interspecies interactions ===
The thalli of ''Batrachospermum'' are a food source for aquatic invertebrates, including [[Amphipoda|amphipods]], [[snail]]s, and [[aquatic insect]] larvae.<ref name=":2" /> In some studies, they have been found in the gut content of almost half of the examined individuals.<ref name=":9" />

The [[silk]]-like secretions that bind the threads of ''Batrachospermum'' are used to build shelters by some [[Chironomidae|chironomidic]] larvae. Shelters made from different species of ''Batrachospermum'' have slightly different structures.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sheath |first1=Robert G. |last2=Müller |first2=Kirsten M. |last3=Colbo |first3=Murray H. |last4=Cole |first4=Kathleen M. |year=1996 |title=Incorporation of freshwater Rhodophyta into the cases of chironomid larvae (Chironomidae, Diptera) from North America |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.0022-3646.1996.00949.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language=en |volume=32 |issue=6 |pages=949–952 |doi=10.1111/j.0022-3646.1996.00949.x |bibcode=1996JPcgy..32..949S |issn=0022-3646|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The gelatinous sheath serves as a habitat for [[Periphyton|periphytic]] algae, such as ''{{Interlanguage link|Chrysodesmis gloeophila|pl|Chrysodesmis gloeophila}}''.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Guiry |first1=G. M. |last2=Guiry |first2=M. D. |year=2012 |title=Chrysodesmis Starmach, 1970: 192 |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/genus/detail/?genus_id=H5ed7a69b30b1aa44 |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=www.algaebase.org |publisher=National University of Ireland |publication-place=Galway}}</ref> Some algae, such as the red algae ''Balbiania'' and ''Sirodotia'', can also grow directly on the gelatinous thalli of ''Batrachospermum''.<ref name=":12" />

== Life cycle ==
The ''Batrachospermum'', like other red algae, undergoes an [[alternation of generations]]. The life cycle involves one [[haploid]] generation of [[gametophyte]] (typically described as the actual individual of ''Batrachospermum'') and two [[diploid]] generations of [[sporophyte]]s – [[carposporophyte]] and ''Chantransia'' (or pseudochantransia).

The ''Chantransia'' stage is annual. ''Chantransia'' can produce monospores or, through [[Meiosis|meiotic]] division, produce gametophyte thalli growing on it, without releasing tetraspores.<ref name=":2" /> Gametophytes live for a short period – from late autumn to early spring in tropical regions or slightly longer in temperate zones.<ref name=":5" /> However, in certain conditions, they can also be perennial.<ref name=":4" /> The production of gametophytes may be associated with [[photoperiodism]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brawley |first1=Susan H. |last2=Johnson |first2=Ladd E. |year=1992 |title=Gametogenesis, gametes and zygotes: An ecological perspective on sexual reproduction in the algae |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00071619200650241 |journal=British Phycological Journal |language=en |volume=27 |issue=3 |pages=233–252 |doi=10.1080/00071619200650241 |issn=0007-1617}}</ref> Gametophytes produce male gametes – [[Spermatozoon|spermatozoids]] and female gametes – [[Carpogonium|carpogonia]] (which are essentially identical to [[Oogonium|oogonia]]). Some species (e.g., ''Batrachospermum boryanum'') are [[dioecious]], while others are [[monoicous]].<ref name=":2" /> In some species (e.g., ''B. delicatulum'', also known as ''B. gelatinosum''), both monoicious and dioecious individuals occur.<ref name=":5" /> Both types of gametes are non-motile – spermatozoids are released into the water and carried by its movement, while carpogonia remain on the parent plant, germinating into carposporophytes after fertilization. Carposporophytes, originating from the [[zygote]], are diploids. Due to their inconspicuous appearance and occurrence on gametophytes, they were once considered parasites.<ref name=":8" /> However, sometimes they detach from the gametophyte, serving as [[Diaspore (botany)|diaspores]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hambrook |first1=Julie A. |last2=Sheath |first2=Robert G. |year=1991 |title=Reproductive ecology of the freshwater red alga Batrachospermum boryanum Sirodot in a temperature headwater stream |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00038837 |journal=Hydrobiologia |language=en |volume=218 |issue=3 |pages=233–246 |doi=10.1007/BF00038837 |issn=0018-8158|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Carposporophytes produce [[carpospore]]s released into the water, from which the ''Chantransia'' stage germinates.<ref name=":3" /> An exception is ''Batrachospermum brasiliense'', in which there is no carposporophyte, and the ''Chantransia'' stage grows directly from the fertilized carpogonium.<ref name=":3" /> Since the gametophyte grows on the ''Chantransia'', the carposporophyte on the gametophyte, and the carpospores can germinate on the parent plant, their common body can be considered a kind of [[Chimera (genetics)|chimera]].<ref name=":13">{{Cite journal |last1=von Stosch |first1=H. A. |last2=Theil |first2=Gisela |year=1979 |title=A New Mode of Life History in the Freshwater Red Algal Genus Batrachospermum |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2442632 |journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=66 |issue=1 |pages=105–107|doi=10.1002/j.1537-2197.1979.tb06200.x |jstor=2442632 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

For many years, it was believed that the only diploid stage in the development of ''Batrachospermum'' is the zygote, which immediately undergoes meiosis, making the carposporophyte [[Haplontic|haplont]].<ref name=":8" /> Such information is still presented in relatively modern studies,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sharma |first=O. P. |title=Textbook of algae |date=2007 |publisher=Tata McGraw-Hill Education |isbn=978-0-07-451928-8 |edition=19 |location=New Delhi |pages=63–65}}</ref> despite the fact that since the mid-20th century, it has been discovered that successive species representing this life cycle model (supposedly represented by the genus ''Nemalion'') actually have a model similar to most other red algae (typified by ''Polysiphonia'').<ref>{{Cite book |title=Advance of phycology in Japan |date=1975 |publisher=Junk |isbn=978-90-6193-026-6 |editor-last=Tokida |editor-first=Jun |location=The Hague |page=146 |editor-last2=Hirose |editor-first2=Hiroyuki}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Szweykowska |first1=Alicja |title=Botanika. Systematyka |last2=Szweykowski |first2=Jerzy |publisher=Wydawnictwo Naukowe PWN |year=2007 |isbn=978-83-01-13945-2 |location=Warsaw |pages=pl}}</ref> Additional misunderstandings arose from the fact that after meiosis in ''Chantransia'' (or pseudochantransia), only one cell ([[meiospore]]) gives rise to a new individual, while the rest degenerate, which is unusual in algae. Moreover, the meiospore is not released but germinates on the parent plant. It was only in the late 1960s and early 1970s that it was proven that the nuclei of ''Batrachospermum'' and ''Lemanea'' gametophytes contain half of the DNA of the nuclei of individuals from the supposed genus ''Pesudochantransia''.<ref name=":13" />

== Uses ==
Unlike some marine red algae, ''Batrachospermum'' is not used in cooking. There are few reports of the anti-inflammatory properties of ''B. atrum'' used in folk medicine at the foothills of the [[Himalayas]] ([[Arunachal Pradesh]]).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Namsa |first1=Nima D. |last2=Tag |first2=Hui |last3=Mandal |first3=M. |last4=Kalita |first4=P. |last5=Das |first5=A.K. |year=2009 |title=An ethnobotanical study of traditional anti-inflammatory plants used by the Lohit community of Arunachal Pradesh, India |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0378874109004322 |journal=Journal of Ethnopharmacology |language=en |volume=125 |issue=2 |pages=234–245 |doi=10.1016/j.jep.2009.07.004|pmid=19607898 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Due to its environmental requirements, representatives of this genus found in [[Poland]] are considered when determining the {{Interlanguage link|River Macrophyte Index|pl|Makrofitowy Indeks Rzeczny}}, with values of W=6 (indicating a preference for mesotrophic waters) and L=2 (indicating an average range of [[ecological tolerance]]).<ref>{{Cite book |title=Makrofitowa metoda oceny rzek: podręcznik metodyczny do oceny i klasyfikacji stanu ekologicznego wód płynących w oparciu o rośliny wodne |date=2010 |publisher=Bogucki Wydawnictwo Naukowe |isbn=978-83-61320-81-4 |editor-last=Szoszkiewicz |editor-first=Krzysztof |location=Poznań |pages=60–68 |language=pl}}</ref>
